title: Bill To Email rejects a valid 32-character address
reason: Final verification failed: "no error message is shown under the Bill To Email field"

verdict.title: Bill To Email rejects a valid 32-character address
verdict.oneLiner: The requested Bill To Email remains in the field, but the form incorrectly shows an error beneath it.
verdict.rootCause: The form applies a 30-character limit to the Bill To Email field. The requested valid email address is 32 characters long, so the form shows an error even though the address is valid.
verdict.suggestion: Update the Bill To Email validation to allow standard valid email-address lengths, then rerun the check with accounts-receivable@example.test.

attempts.agentSummary:
I've made the fix. The only other places that mention the old message are Gremlin's own files, which I haven't touched.

The root cause was the shared `email` validator in `lib/schemas.ts:47`. It capped addresses at 30 characters with `.max(30)`, so a valid 32-character address like `accounts-receivable@example.test` showed a length error. Both Bill From and Bill To use this validator. I raised the cap to 254, the longest address the email standard (RFC 5321) allows, and updated the error message to match. The format check and the 5-character minimum are unchanged.

I haven't run Gremlin, Kane or the app, as this session's rules say; Gremlin will re-run the flow in a browser to check the fix.

I fixed the crash in `lib/helpers.ts`, but I haven't seen it work: the type check passed with no errors in that file, my quick Node check of the new logic needed approval and didn't run, and as instructed I didn't run the app, Gremlin or Kane.

The page crashed because a total of 1,000,000,000 × 10,000,000 = 1e16 is above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. `formatPriceToString` (called from `calculateTotal` in `contexts/ChargesContext.tsx`) passed that total to `number-to-words`' `toWords()`, which threw a RangeError inside a `useEffect` and took the whole form down. I added an `integerToWords` helper that uses BigInt to spell out amounts above that limit one three-digit group at a time, so 1e16 becomes "Ten quadrillion". `formatPriceToString` now returns blank words instead of throwing when an amount is infinite or above about 10^36, too big to spell out.

The bug title is about the email field, but this flow tests the large-total crash, so that's what I fixed. The email-length change from attempt 1 is still in `lib/schemas.ts`; I left it alone.
